decision: held: the two declared meta-analyses that could support credit (32154768 muscle damage, 32359762 body weight) have no open full text; their abstracts report no per-trial dose, form or included-trial list, so rule 2 dose verification is impossible. The accessible 32958033 is a mixed-design narrative review and is completed as a non-credit context. OA retry 2026-10-28: OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Europe PMC report no open copy of 32154768 or 32359762.
summary: 32958033 (11 studies, 1 to 4.5 g/day for 12-24 weeks, mixed designs) shows population-dependent effects and higher fasting TMAO; it cannot carry credit. 32154768 (7 RCTs, less soreness) and 32359762 (37 RCTs, -1.21 kg body weight) look favorable from their abstracts but cannot be verified for dose or included trials, so the record stays held rather than reference-only (no frozen dependants).

identity.preparation: Oral L-carnitine, mostly L-carnitine L-tartrate (LCLT); salt mass and carnitine base not equated

population.description: 11 studies (2002-2020) in healthy humans, from young athletes to aged women and centenarians, supplemented >=12 weeks.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review without meta-analysis; PICOS admitted randomized controlled, non-randomized controlled and non-randomized non-controlled designs.

outcomes.name: Muscle carnitine, performance and body-composition effects vary by population and cointervention; 24 weeks did not change muscle strength in aged women; centenarian muscle mass and effort tolerance improved
Fasting plasma TMAO increased, without change in measured inflammatory or oxidative-stress markers

limitations: Mixed randomized and non-randomized designs; narrative synthesis only, not a pooled RCT estimate. Not credit-bearing.
Dose range is 1-4 g/day in the abstract but 1 to 4.5 g/day in Results; discrepancy retained.

Declared meta-analyses 32154768 (7 RCTs, exercise-induced muscle damage; soreness improved at 0-96 h) and 32359762 (37 RCTs, 2292 participants; body weight WMD -1.21 kg, -1.73 to -0.68) have no open full text; abstracts give no per-trial regimens, forms or included-trial lists, so no context could be completed for them.
Do not transfer centenarian findings to ordinary healthy adults or add overlapping older-women reports as independent cohorts.
Despite restrictive abstract wording, the source table includes carbohydrate and leucine cointerventions; these cannot be ignored.
Physical dosage form is not specified uniformly by the source table; no capsule assumption.

Included-study identifiers are now bound to this source's actual included-study rows/explicit inclusion references (Tables Tab1 explicit included-study row citations), with live NIH title/content identity checks. They are publication pointers, not independent-cohort counts, per-primary-study scoring approvals, preparation equivalence or new efficacy evidence. Exact unindexed source citations remain retained; no missing PMID is invented.
